name: שִׁמְעוֹן
summary: Jacob’s second son by Leah, and the tribe named from him, whose host under Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai marched with Reuben’s camp when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 10:19). Leah named him for what Yahweh had done: “because Yahweh has heard (שָׁמַע) that I am hated, he has given me this one also” (Gen 29:33). It is the verb שָׁמַע with the ending ־וֹן. Simeon and Levi avenged Dinah at Shechem (Gen 34:25), and Jacob said of them “I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel” (Gen 49:5–7): Simeon’s lot fell inside Judah’s (Jos 19:1, 9). The name is borne by a man of Ezra’s day (Ezr 10:31), and in the New Testament, as Συμεών, by the righteous man who took the child Jesus in his arms (Luk 2:25), a forefather of Jesus (Luk 3:30), and a teacher at Antioch (Act 13:1); the tribe is sealed in Rev 7:7.

evidence.note: “Because Yahweh has heard (שָׁמַע) that I am hated, he has given me this one also; and she called his name שִׁמְעוֹן.”
Over the host of the tribe of the sons of שִׁמְעוֹן, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, take their swords against Shechem.
“Simeon and Levi are brothers … I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.”
The second lot came out for Simeon; their inheritance was within the inheritance of Judah.
Shimeon, among the sons of Harim who had taken foreign wives.
Συμεών, “righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel”.
Of the tribe of Simeon twelve thousand sealed.
The same reason given for Ishmael’s name: “because Yahweh has heard (שָׁמַע) your affliction”.
Rachel names Dan: “God … has also heard (שָׁמַע) my voice”; Leah’s and Rachel’s sons are named for God’s hearing.

note: The verb in Gen 29:33 fixes the name’s meaning as the text gives it; the ־וֹן ending is read as forming a noun or diminutive (“a hearing”), so “one heard” rests on the naming, not the form. TIPNR’s Simeon@Gen.29.33 record carries the tribe and the gentilic שִׁמְעֹנִי (v.ed.ap), so that key is listed here. Peter is called Συμεών in Act 15:14 and 2Pe 1:1 and the many NT Σίμων are the same Hebrew name in Greek dress, but TIPNR files them under Peter and Simon; they are left off.
